duty_3a_marker_detection_fixed_or_derive.why: There is nothing to derive it FROM: the state file only ever authors POSITIVE status. The one plausible derivation — reusing non-landed ladder[].status values — is self-weakening: it empties out exactly when every slice is landed, i.e. when a board is most likely stale, and it could only ever carry the STATE FILE's vocabulary, never the BOARD's, which is the thing under test.
duty_3a_marker_detection_fixed_or_derive.what_it_CANNOT_catch: 'pending', 'TBD', 'queued', 'awaiting review', 'blocked on X', '0/5 arms green', an em-dash, an empty cell, or a row that is simply months out of date in upbeat wording — ALL PASS. It is a prose regex: it detects the phrasings someone thought of, and a board that goes stale in a new phrasing goes stale silently.
duty_3a_marker_detection_fixed_or_derive.false_positives_it_will_produce: The markers match anywhere in the status cell, so a landed slice whose close prose reads 'closed while in-flight work was parked' IS flagged. Intended strictness, but it has a cost. 'next' is deliberately whole-cell only, never bare \bnext\b — in a status cell it is a pointer word and a false positive HARD-BLOCKS A LAND.
duty_3a_marker_detection_fixed_or_derive.trust_boundary: Trust the row-scoped SHA check, not the vocabulary check: it is derived, has no vocabulary, and is the half that would actually have caught the Slice 39 incident. This limitation is recorded in the code as a comment, not only here.
duty_3a_marker_detection_fixed_or_derive.self_inflicted_false_negative_caught: The obvious clause-cut-at-punctuation reader parsed 'Ladder remaining: 39.5, 40' as {39.5} and would have truncated 40.5 -> 40 — THIS UNIT'S OWN DEFECT CLASS re-introduced inside its own fix. Replaced with an ID-list reader; fixtures P/Q arm both directions.

absent_or_malformed_state_file_policy: ABSENT -> cross-read skipped and ANNOUNCED ('note ... cross-read (TC-133) DID NOT RUN'), not a failure: a hard fail would redden boards predating the single writer, a silent skip rebuilds the blind spot. PRESENT BUT MALFORMED (bad JSON, not an object, missing or WRONG-TYPED landed/ladder/remaining_ladder, ladder not an array of objects) -> HARD fail with a preflight-recognised prefix. Also hard-fail: board unreadable, no ladder table when a state file exists, python3 absent.
